responsibilities: Frame measurable outcomes and failure conditions.
Define authority, invariants, change classes, architecture boundaries, and evidence.
Govern Git, testing, artifact traceability, and operational claims.
Provide deterministic isolation, build, delivery, identity, secret, provenance, promotion, and rollback boundaries.
Reduce organizational and environment friction through reproducible setup, discoverable contracts, and actionable failures.
Prevent higher autonomy from exceeding demonstrated factory substrate maturity.
Trace adopted recommendations to controls, artifacts, tests, evidence, status, and known gaps.
Keep design intent, architecture boundaries, execution traces, and judgment review independently inspectable.
Use probabilistic review to discover risks while deterministic controls and accountable humans retain authority.
Define bounded agent roles, workflows, tools, context, traces, and human gates.
Separate deterministic controls from probabilistic decisions.
Constrain model and tool authority by declared contracts.
Define frontend, backend, API, accessibility, browser, and product-analytics boundaries.
Preserve typed contracts and explicit failure behavior across client and server.
Require user-visible workflow evidence.
Define data ownership, lineage, quality, migrations, retention, and recovery.
Keep destructive changes approval-bound and rollback-capable.
Link derived data and claims to source evidence.
Turn traces into narrow learning candidates without direct trusted-state mutation.
Replay, evaluate, shadow, approve, canary, promote, and roll back candidates.
Keep evaluators and promotion authority independent from execution.
Define audience, positioning, proof-backed claims, launch assets, economics, and feedback routes.
Keep publishing and spending under accountable human authority.
Connect market evidence and product outcomes back to planning.

invariants.enforcement: authority-matrix
invariants.statement: Agents cannot ratify constitutional changes.
invariants.verification: protocol validation and approval evidence

invariants.enforcement: workflow separation
invariants.statement: The executor cannot be the sole evaluator or promoter of its governed change.
invariants.verification: trace and approval evidence

invariants.enforcement: external credential broker
invariants.statement: Production credentials remain outside agent sandboxes.
invariants.verification: security audit and sandbox test

invariants.enforcement: artifact digest and provenance check
invariants.statement: The same immutable artifact is promoted across environments.
invariants.verification: promotion record

invariants.enforcement: trace schema and delivery gates
invariants.statement: Every governed change is traceable from outcome through observed result.
invariants.verification: complete trace linkage

invariants.enforcement: quarantined learning workflow
invariants.statement: Learning cannot directly modify production, constitutional policy, or trusted evaluators.
invariants.verification: promotion evidence

invariants.enforcement: test workflow
invariants.statement: Testing advances one level at a time and reruns a failed level after root-cause correction.
invariants.verification: ordered test evidence

invariants.enforcement: readiness review
invariants.statement: Operational claims require current executable evidence.
invariants.verification: evidence reference

invariants.enforcement: dataset digest and calibration gate
invariants.statement: A probabilistic evaluator cannot score governed holdout cases until it qualifies against human reference labels for the same dataset revision.
invariants.verification: qualified calibration report

invariants.enforcement: telemetry contract and event validation
invariants.statement: Telemetry cannot persist secrets by default or use high-cardinality correlation identifiers as metric dimensions.
invariants.verification: privacy, correlation, and cardinality tests

invariants.enforcement: context policy, delegation binding, memory lifecycle, authority matrix, and persistent-store validation
invariants.statement: Retrieval, context assembly, and memory writes cannot expand authority; delegated context binds an immutable delegation and in-scope repository sources; trusted memory requires independent human approval and source provenance.
invariants.verification: delegated identity, scope, source, authority, provenance, lifecycle, expiry, and context-budget tests

invariants.enforcement: resolved project authority and delegation validators
invariants.statement: A parent run must explicitly claim delegation authority, every claimed action must be a subset of its resolved project role and identity grants, and delegated authority cannot exceed that validated parent authority, the child project role binding, or the declared authority ceiling.
invariants.verification: missing delegation claim, forged parent, and child authority subset fixtures

invariants.enforcement: agent-run chain, tool, role, budget, deadline, and bidirectional normalized-scope validation
invariants.statement: Tool grants do not imply approval or promotion authority, and a child cannot broaden delegated authority, tools, budget, deadline, expiry, or scope.
invariants.verification: invalid authority, tool, budget, deadline, and forbidden-scope fixtures

invariants.enforcement: delegation, agent-run chain, and checkpoint binding validation
invariants.statement: Every delegation has an expiry or termination condition, every child run traces to exactly one parent delegation, and every checkpoint binds to that exact delegation and child run.
invariants.verification: parent-child and mismatched checkpoint fixtures

invariants.enforcement: delegation policy and aggregate budget validation
invariants.statement: Cancellation propagates to active child work and child budgets aggregate within the parent budget.
invariants.verification: cancellation and aggregate budget fixtures

invariants.enforcement: fail-closed delegation and message validation
invariants.statement: A failed authority check blocks execution, and messages cannot mutate governed state directly.
invariants.verification: invalid authority and message fixtures

invariants.enforcement: assigned-identity lease and transactional SQLite journals
invariants.statement: A child runtime operation requires the active lease issued to its assigned identity, and action, message, checkpoint, and runtime-event sequences are append-only and contiguous.
invariants.verification: forged lease, sequence gap, duplicate record, and concurrent claim tests

invariants.enforcement: deterministic replay verifier and runtime policy
invariants.statement: Checkpoint and runtime-event digest chains must replay to the persisted lifecycle state; runtime coordination cannot approve, promote, or authenticate external identities.
invariants.verification: tampered event, broken checkpoint chain, cancellation, expiry, and replay-state tests

invariants.enforcement: learning policy, observation validation, artifact-byte binding, and append-only journal replay
invariants.statement: Counterfactual replay and shadow learning are side-effect-free, digest-bound to immutable candidate artifacts, and cannot mutate governed targets.
invariants.verification: side-effect, artifact mutation, row mutation, event mutation, and replay tests

invariants.enforcement: learning evaluation, approval, promotion, rollback, and identity-separation contracts
invariants.statement: A learning candidate requires independent evaluation, kind-specific accountable approvals, and a separate promoter; promotion emits an immutable packet and never applies the target mutation.
invariants.verification: self-evaluation, missing evidence, missing approval, self-promotion, promotion packet, and rollback tests

invariants.enforcement: qualification policy, active Ed25519 trust anchors, immutable bundle validation, and cumulative gate evaluation
invariants.statement: A hosted maturity claim requires current independently signed evidence bound to one project, environment, artifact, trusted source, payload digest, and cumulative maturity gate.
invariants.verification: forged signature, payload mutation, payload deletion, stale evidence, trust, project, environment, artifact, and cumulative-gate tests

invariants.enforcement: qualification policy authority constants and immutable report contract
invariants.statement: Qualification is advisory and cannot mutate the canonical maturity assessment, promote an artifact, deploy a release, or substitute mechanism availability for hosted operational evidence.
invariants.verification: maturity immutability, authority, empty-trust, and non-claim tests

invariants.enforcement: autonomy policy, pinned qualification consumption, class registry, and deterministic effective-autonomy calculation
invariants.statement: Effective autonomy is the minimum of verified hosted maturity, project autonomy ceiling, selected autonomy-class maximum, and active certification level; a certification can consume but cannot create, update, or reinterpret maturity.
invariants.verification: operand ordering, ceiling, digest pinning, and maturity-immutability tests

invariants.enforcement: hard-stop policy and append-only governance records
invariants.statement: Invalid qualification, expiry, suspension, revocation, contradiction, or exhausted incident budget resolves effective autonomy to no authority.
invariants.verification: invalid qualification, expiry, suspension, revocation, contradiction, and budget-exhaustion fixtures

invariants.enforcement: simulation policy constants, structured work-item validation, hash-chained replay, and simulation reports
invariants.statement: P5.1 matching, simulation, certification replay, and incident accounting are deterministic and side-effect-free; they cannot mutate a workspace or create a pull request.
invariants.verification: scope, tool, check, equivalence, event-chain, incident-accounting, CLI, and determinism tests

invariants.enforcement: canonical project authority registry, signed qualification re-verification, signed authority-source evidence, certification lifecycle replay, exact effective-autonomy, match, and simulation recomputation, short-lived lease, and fail-closed issuance
invariants.statement: A P5.2 pull-request authority lease requires a repository-owned canonical project authority source, signed-bundle P4.7 re-evaluation, an independently signed complete governance-source statement bound to that source, an active certification lifecycle replay, exact trusted-source recomputation of every derived report, and current hard-stop checks.
invariants.verification: qualified lease, caller-selected policy or ceiling, forged authority statement, fabricated certification or report, foreign qualification, future lifecycle, scope mismatch, failed simulation, expiry, suspension, revocation, and budget-window tests

invariants.enforcement: supervised execution, independently signed workspace, file-change, test, evaluation, hosted Git evidence, and repository URL prefix, authority-source and lease validation, packet reconstruction, current qualification re-verification, immutable PR packet contracts, and exact provider-response binding
invariants.statement: A supervised autonomous pull request requires a current reconstructed lease, exact source execution and packet binding, ordered test evidence, independent evaluation, verified hosted Git governance, and external identity; humans retain merge and release authority.
invariants.verification: fabricated packet or structural lease, expired lease, workspace, file, test, and evaluation drift, positive SHA-1 and SHA-256 Git object formats, diff binding, test ordering, evaluator separation, forged hosted-control evidence, provider packet-digest, repository, branch, revision, unrelated URL host or path, and diff mismatch, merge, deploy, and maturity-authority tests

invariants.enforcement: context-policy graph-selection controls and context assembler validation
invariants.statement: Context assembly must never inject a wholesale knowledge or protocol graph; graph context is query-matched, source-bounded, authority-filtered, and capped by policy.
invariants.verification: wildcard, empty-term, and over-limit graph-context negative tests

invariants.enforcement: L3-only canary simulation, exact signed canary-authority evidence, trusted-source lease reconstruction, current lifecycle and non-future-dated governance revalidation, signed provider evidence with a reserved deployment identifier, runtime-owned canonical durable plan, execution-id, and packet claim, immutable execution packet, accepted response, and rollback packet, durable start-response and deadline registration and scheduling, immediate watchdog-installation rollback, restart-safe runtime-clock due-work sweep with per-record isolation and terminal expiry state, atomic rollback claim for every executor with full runtime activation-window validation before claim and provider invocation, runtime-time deadline predicates, shorter claim timeout and unchanged-packet recovery inside the original authorization window, observing-state-only telemetry, fresh signed deployment observation, evaluation-time threshold checks, automatic rollback adapter invocation, exact rollback response binding, and explicit promotion denial
invariants.statement: P5.3 canary authority requires current non-future-dated L3 qualification and governance checks, canonical project authority, an active explicitly canary-capable L3 certification, exact signed plan authority, bounded traffic and duration, signed provider identity, secret, telemetry, immutable-artifact, promotion-gate, and rollback evidence, runtime-owned one-shot plan and packet consumption, current governance revalidation, provider-reserved deployment identity, durable start-response and observation watchdog registration, immediate rollback when watchdog installation fails, canonical accepted-response and rollback-packet persistence, runtime-clock recovery without caller-selected time, atomic claiming and full requested-at-through-required-by runtime validation for every rollback executor, exact response, deployment, and observation binding, terminal-state observation denial, and automatic recoverable rollback on any start uncertainty, threshold, duration, stale-telemetry, or missing-telemetry breach without early activation, renewing the original rollback authority, or allowing one expired record to block other due work; no canary result authorizes promotion or full rollout.
invariants.verification: L2 and non-canary-class denial, cross-plan authority rejection, fabricated lease or packet, alternate-store and caller-time API exclusion, sequential, concurrent, repackaged-plan, and direct rollback-executor replay, current suspension, future-dated governance checks and rollback packets, stale or forged provider evidence, malformed or failed start recovery, response target and deployment mismatch, caller-substituted accepted response, terminal-state observation rejection, unsigned or foreign observation, delayed and missing telemetry, watchdog-installation failure, pre-provider rollback expiry, early deadline-claim denial, durable claimed-start and exact-packet stale-rollback recovery, expired rollback non-renewal, expired-record sweep isolation, traffic and duration bounds, automatic rollback, healthy non-promotion, CLI, determinism, and canonical-readiness tests

constraints: The initial product accepts customer feedback but must not accept credentials, regulated data, or proprietary source-code uploads.
Humans retain merge, release, deployment, learning-promotion, and architecture-exception authority.
The first milestone uses local or free-tier infrastructure and does not require autonomous production deployment.
The initial product is a single repository using TypeScript, Next.js, and PostgreSQL.
Billing, enterprise tenant administration, autonomous production deployment, model-weight fine-tuning, and application-user memory are initial non-goals.
profile.mission: Help B2B SaaS founders, product teams, and support teams turn customer feedback into traceable product signals, prioritized issues, completed fixes, and release communication.
profile.name: SignalDesk

failure: SignalDesk loses source evidence or merges unrelated feedback without an owner-visible explanation.
Customer feedback or workspace data is exposed outside its authorized product boundary.
An agent merges, releases, deploys, promotes learning, or overrides architecture without the required human decision.
The product cannot reconstruct why a signal was prioritized, changed, rejected, fixed, or communicated.
success: An authenticated team member can capture customer feedback and convert it into a traceable canonical signal through the product interface.
Repeated feedback can be grouped without losing its original sources, customer context, or evidence.
A product owner can promote a signal into a prioritized issue with an explicit rationale and accountable decision history.
A team can track an accepted issue through implementation, verification, completion, and customer-facing release communication.
The first product milestone passes its ordered tests and can be operated through the product interface without database or background-terminal inspection.
